conventions.scaleSource: meta.height (relative to an average man = 1.0); every figure fills the same box, the game scales by height
conventions.pivot: feet centre on the baseline (figures), neck base (heads)

style: STYLE: traditional Mithila (Madhubani) painting from Bihar, in the manner of old village wall paintings, hand-painted with natural pigments: lampblack, indigo, turmeric yellow, saffron, madder red, leaf green, ochre and terracotta. Bold black double outlines on every shape, flat colour fills filled with fine hand-drawn patterns (lines, dots, small triangles, lotus and fish motifs), slight pigment texture, no photographic shading, no gradients, no glow, no 3D rendering. Figures in strict side profile with one large almond-shaped eye, stylised elongated bodies, ornamented clothing. Reverent, dignified, storybook clarity. No text, no letters, no signature, no watermark.

assets.name: Rama
assets.prompt:
Character design sheet of Rama (prince), the same figure three times side by side: (1) standing upright, at rest, (2) walking steadily, mid-step, (3) a characteristic action pose. Prince Rama of Ayodhya, the hero, eldest son of King Dasharatha; noble, calm and gentle, a peerless archer. Shown in the prince stage of the story. Appearance: a human figure, tall, medium build, light indigo-blue skin, long almond eye, soft brows, clean-shaven, Vaishnava tilak (vertical U mark) on the forehead, tall ornate golden crown, deep indigo dhoti with gold borders and a repeating row of small lotus motifs, princely gold jewellery (earrings, necklaces, armlets, anklets), carries the Kodanda, a tall curved bow, and a quiver of arrows. All figures face RIGHT in strict side profile. Each figure is whole: top of head or crown near the top edge, feet resting on one shared level ground line near the bottom edge, nothing cropped, nothing overlapping. Background: one flat, perfectly uniform solid magenta (#FF00FF) colour filling the whole image, no texture, no floor, no shadow, nothing else.
STYLE: traditional Mithila (Madhubani) painting from Bihar, in the manner of old village wall paintings, hand-painted with natural pigments: lampblack, indigo, turmeric yellow, saffron, madder red, leaf green, ochre and terracotta. Bold black double outlines on every shape, flat colour fills filled with fine hand-drawn patterns (lines, dots, small triangles, lotus and fish motifs), slight pigment texture, no photographic shading, no gradients, no glow, no 3D rendering. Figures in strict side profile with one large almond-shaped eye, stylised elongated bodies, ornamented clothing. Reverent, dignified, storybook clarity. No text, no letters, no signature, no watermark.
